_note: FICTIONAL sample data for user-research-synthesis. Companies, people and links are invented; notes.granola.ai/d/sample-* links are placeholders.

research_questions.text: How do new admins get their first workflow live, and where do they stall?
What do admins expect from the first-week setup checklist?
Who else gets involved before a workspace is rolled out to the team?

meetings.detail: listed by folder for the study period

transcript.text:
Microphone: Thanks for making time, Maya. How did you get your first workflow live?
System audio: Honestly, it took a week. I got stuck on the very first screen, connecting our shipment database. I asked Kwame in finance for the login and waited two days.
Microphone: What were you trying to get done?
System audio: I want the Monday hand-offs between dispatch and billing to run without me chasing people, and without filing an IT ticket every time.
Microphone: Wouldn't a progress bar make you more likely to finish the checklist?
System audio: Yeah, I guess a progress bar would be nice.
Microphone: What would a great first day look like?
System audio: Seeing one workflow run end to end on day one. Then I'd trust it.
Microphone: Anything else about the checklist?
System audio: Not really. Vellicor is small, so it's mostly me.

notes.text: Maya (Vellicor Freight) stalled on connecting the shipment database; the credentials are held by finance. Wants the Monday hand-offs automated.

transcript.text:
Microphone: Can you walk me through setting up your workspace?
System audio: Sure. I shared my screen with Hana last time, but basically I skipped the templates. They looked like they were for bigger companies.
Microphone: Where did it get hard?
System audio: Connecting the patient-booking system. The API key lives with our IT contractor, so everything stopped there.
Microphone: How do you handle the reminders today?
System audio: We still run the reminders from a shared spreadsheet. Until I trust the workflow, the spreadsheet stays.
Microphone: Would single sign-on matter for you?
System audio: We don't need single sign-on. We're eleven people.
Microphone: What's the job you hired us for?
System audio: Getting patient reminders out without someone copying rows every morning.

notes.text: Tomasz shared his screen. He opened the template gallery, closed it after a few seconds, and built the workflow from a blank canvas. Stalled at the booking-system connection (API key held by their IT contractor).

transcript.text:
Microphone: How did rollout start at your company?
System audio: At Hobblestead we can't connect anything until IT signs off, and the warehouse system credentials sit with them.
Microphone: So connecting the first source was the slow part?
System audio: Connecting the warehouse system took us nine days, mostly waiting.
Microphone: What would you want from the setup checklist?
System audio: I need the checklist to show me what my team still has to do, not just my own steps. And single sign-on has to be on it, our security review asks for it first.
Microphone: Who else had to approve the purchase?
System audio: Finance had to approve the plan before we could invite anyone. That's just how we work.

notes.text: Priya Halvorsen, Hobblestead Foods. IT gate before any connection; SSO required by security review; finance approves the plan.

transcript.text:
Microphone: How did setup go?
System audio: Slow at the start. Our client calendars sit in an account only the founder can log into, so I couldn't connect them.
Microphone: What were you hoping to automate?
System audio: Weekly client status hand-offs, so the team stops pinging me for updates.
Microphone: And until then?
System audio: A shared spreadsheet, honestly. Everyone updates a row.
Microphone: So a progress bar would help, right?
System audio: Sure, that would probably help.

notes.text: Dev from Tindleforge Agency. Calendars locked to the founder's account.

transcript.text:
Microphone: Tell me about the first week.
System audio: The first week was mostly waiting on credentials for the scheduling system. Our ops lead holds them.
Microphone: If something goes wrong, who should we contact?
System audio: Just send it to ruth.adeyemi@pridmoxa.example and I'll forward it.
Microphone: What about the checklist?
System audio: I ignore progress bars, to be honest. I want the checklist to list single sign-on and who on my team hasn't logged in yet.
Microphone: What would make day one feel successful?
System audio: One reminder going out for real on day one. That's the moment I'd show my boss.

notes.text: Ruth shared her screen. She skipped the template gallery and started from a blank canvas. She asked where the SSO settings are. Waiting on scheduling-system credentials from the ops lead.

transcript.text:
Microphone: What's your setup like today?
System audio: We keep the purchase-order hand-offs in a shared spreadsheet until the automation proves itself.
Microphone: What do you expect from the checklist?
System audio: Single sign-on first, then a view of which teammates still have tasks open.
Microphone: Anything missing from what you've seen?
System audio: The pricing page doesn't say which plan has audit logs. I had to ask sales.

notes.text: Sunniva shared her screen. She connected the print-queue database herself in about ten minutes using the setup guide. She said she wants hand-offs between the studio and the print floor to run on their own. She did not open the template gallery and started from a blank canvas. Follow-up: +44 20 7946 0958.

transcript.text:
Microphone: How did the first connection go?
System audio: It was slow, I needed someone else's password.

notes.text: Leo Marchetti. Declined consent at the end of the session.

findings.statement: New admins stall at connecting the first data source, before they build any workflow.
Admins skip the template gallery and build their first workflow from a blank canvas.

surprise.assumption: Templates are the main way new admins get started.

findings.statement: Admins want the setup checklist to show what their teammates still have to do.
A progress bar would motivate admins to finish the setup checklist.
Finance approves the plan before a sales-assisted workspace is rolled out.
Admins expect single sign-on to be a step in the setup checklist.
Get recurring team hand-offs running on their own, without chasing people or filing IT tickets.
The credentials for the first data source are held by someone else in the company.
Keep the hand-off in a shared spreadsheet until the workflow has earned trust.
See one workflow run end to end on day one.
The pricing page does not say which plan includes audit logs.

opportunities.statement: Add a progress bar to the setup checklist.
Let admins invite the colleague who holds the credentials to connect the first data source.
Make single sign-on and teammates' open tasks part of the sales-assisted checklist.
Show a 'first workflow ran' moment on day one.
Say on the pricing page which plan includes audit logs.

open_questions.text: Whether IT or security reviews the workspace before rollout; only one participant described an approval step.
